title: Your first task in {name}: ask, read the answer, change it
description: Write what you want in {name}’s box, in your own words, and press Enter. Read the answer and its steps, then ask underneath to change it.
answer: Write what you want in the box, the way you would ask a colleague, and press Enter. {name} answers in the task, showing each step it takes. To change anything, just say so underneath.
pane.title: A first request, answered in {name}
demo.asked: Write a short thank-you note to my neighbour Sam, who watered my plants while I was away.
demo.answer:
Dear Sam,

Thank you so much for watering my plants while I was away. I came back to a balcony in full bloom, and I know that took time and care.

If you’re ever away yourself, I’d be glad to return the favour.

With thanks,
need: A brain that answers. The first time, {name} offers one as soon as you send: see {choose}.
steps: Click where it says {placeholder}: that is the box.
Write what you want, in your own words: what it is, for whom, and in what form. To add a file, drop it on the box, or press + beside it.
Press Enter, or the arrow, to send. Shift and Enter start a new line instead.
Read the answer as it comes. Each step it takes shows above it: open one to see what was read and what came back.
To change something, say it underneath: shorter, in French, as a table. Or press {retry} under your request, to have it answered again.
For something else, start a new task with {new}, so each task keeps to one thing.
good: Under each answer: {copy}, with its formatting, and in {more}, sharing, a Word document or printing.
What you write while {name} works is read before its next step. Escape stops the answer.
Up to three follow-ups come as buttons under the last answer.
Each answer says which brain wrote it, how long it took and what it cost.
fixes: {name} needs a brain first, and shows {first} with the ways to get one. See {choose}.
Say what is wrong, underneath, or press {retry}. For figures, ask {name} to work them out: it runs a program rather than guessing.
